name: US government
sents: On August 2, 1964, three North Vietnamese torpedo boats attacked the destroyer USS Maddox while it patrolled in international waters.
The Maddox returned fire, and aircraft from the carrier USS Ticonderoga joined the fight.
On August 4, 1964, North Vietnamese boats attacked the Maddox and the destroyer USS Turner Joy a second time.
On August 5, 1964, American aircraft bombed North Vietnamese naval bases in retaliation.
American officials said two North Vietnamese torpedo boats were sunk in the raids.
Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution on August 7, 1964.
Johnson said the United States sought no wider war.

name: North Vietnam
sents: On August 2, 1964, the American destroyer Maddox entered North Vietnamese waters and was engaged by two patrol boats.
Aircraft from the carrier Ticonderoga then attacked the patrol boats.
Hanoi insisted that no second attack took place on August 4, 1964.
On August 5, 1964, American planes bombed naval bases and an oil depot in the north.
Hanoi said eight of its boats were damaged or sunk in the raids.
On August 7, 1964, the American Congress adopted the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution.
Hanoi protested the raids as an act of war.

name: Retrospective analysis
sents: On August 2, 1964, the Maddox exchanged fire with three torpedo boats after they approached the ship.
Aircraft from the Ticonderoga also attacked the boats.
On August 4, 1964, crews reported a second attack, but later analysis found no evidence that it occurred.
Two days later, American aircraft struck North Vietnamese naval bases.
On August 7, 1964, Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution with two dissenting votes.
Historians later argued that the resolution gave Johnson broad power to expand the war.
